deid_and_dividers.ground_truth: every run of 2+ underscores in the raw text, enumerated independently of the registry
deid_and_dividers.scheme_specific: MIMIC-IV writes de-identification as underscore runs. A corpus using [**Name**] or <REDACTED> needs its own DeidScheme and this number does not transfer to it.

hard_protection_safety.note: edits_touching_a_hard_span is expected to be large and is not an error. It counts legitimate whole replacements — sentence deletion and de-id restyling — which the class permits to operators that declare it.
hard_protection_safety.property: an applied edit may contain a HARD span whole if the operator declares its class; it may never cut one, and may never touch one it has not declared

numeric_value.ground_truth: a token either contains a digit or does not

question: Does the protection registry identify its classes correctly?

section_header.ground_truth: NONE. There is no external header gold, so this is a disclosure rather than a score: how many headers matched the shipped lexicon and how many were guessed.

unvalidated_classes.why: layout judgements with no external reference corpus. Their counts are reported above; their accuracy is not established, and a robustness result that leaned on them would be resting on an unmeasured component.

what_can_and_cannot_be_validated: deid/divider and numeric have a ground truth derivable WITHOUT the registry, so those are measurements. section_header has no external gold and is disclosed by confidence mix. lab_block, dosage and list_marker are layout judgements with no reference and are reported as counts only. Scoring them against themselves would be the failure this file exists to avoid.
why: the registry sets the gap between total_n and eligible_n, so it silently defines every dose denominator; and DEID_PLACEHOLDER is HARD, so under-firing lets an operator corrupt a de-identification marker. Seven producers existed with nothing scoring any of them.
